patch.value: GH-1656: a transaction-owned finalization step for commitItemMutations, so importers keep rollback under the GH-1591 ownership guard

Since GH-1591 (pm-pllp78) commitItemMutations compensates only effects it can prove a step owns. pm-github's importer finalizes exact GitHub source-lifecycle fields (persistImportFidelity, a raw mutateItem op 'import') from the committing transition observer. That event is outside every step's ownership proof, so a failure after finalization reports transaction_partial_mutation and leaves a half-imported tracker. The bulk union accepts only create, update, close and release, and update cannot write native lifecycle fields (closed_at, completed_at) or arbitrary extension fields. Need a journaled step the transaction owns, with its own snapshot and compensation, without weakening the ownership guard. Related to transaction inspection (pm-gh1597).

commitItemMutations accepts a finalization step (field-level document patch or SDK-applied finalize step) that is journaled, attributed to the transaction and compensated by restore exactly like an update step; The GH-1656 reproduction (update step plus finalization, then a failure in the committing observer) restores the item to its pre-batch document with no transaction_partial_mutation; An unowned write by another writer between apply and compensation still refuses with transaction_partial_mutation (negative control); The step is exposed through the public SDK types, docs/SDK.md and the SDK surface snapshot; recovery of an interrupted journal re-applies or adopts the finalization deterministically

value.text: Duplicate check: the create-time detector matched pm-pllp78 (GH-1591, the ownership guard fix, closed). This item is not a recurrence of that defect: the guard stays as shipped, and this asks for a new journaled step type the guard can attribute. pm search for 'finalization commitItemMutations' found only the closed bulk-helper lineage (pm-xm7c, pm-y9hq).

patch.value: An importer finalization inside commitItemMutations is journaled as a step the transaction owns, so a failure after it restores the pre-batch document
Finalization written from the committing observer is unowned, so a later failure reports transaction_partial_mutation and leaves a half-imported tracker
